title: Repairing a Rubber Washer Hose
introduction:
A washer-hose adapter bridges a cut-out damaged section much like a coupling in a garden hose. The important decision comes before the knife: this splice is permitted only on rubber hose. A damaged plastic washer hose needs a new hose instead.

I use the drawings to check the cut-out section and the finished adapter seating. This guide covers the splice on an accessible, confirmed damaged hose; it does not provide route-specific access, plastic-hose replacement or a powered washer-system test.

items.name: Cutting tool and adapter
items.detail: Have a hose-cutting tool capable of making clean cuts; the illustration depicts a utility knife. Use a windshield washer hose adapter to join the cut ends.

items.name: Conditional clamping materials
items.detail: If the difficult-case clamping branch is needed, have black rubber hose of the specified internal diameter and spring clamps available.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Before service around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, using the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could start remotely at any time and cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

requirements.category: If the hose repair requires underhood work

items.name: Cooling fans
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation before underhood work. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; replace it with a new fan as necessary because it can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury. Fans can run with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby to prevent personal injury.

items.name: Rotating engine parts
items.detail: If equipped with engine auto start-stop, keep the ignition off when servicing or working near rotating engine parts. The engine may start automatically with the ignition on and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Safety reference
items.detail: Review the applicable warnings in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

edits.text: NOTE: Use this repair only on rubber washer hose. If a plastic washer hose is damaged, install a new washer hose instead.
edits.why: Hose material determines the repair branch. A neat-looking splice does not make this method suitable for plastic hose.

edits.text: Locate the washer hose and confirm the damaged section before making any cuts.
edits.why: I identify the actual hose damage first so the cutting tool goes to the fault, rather than becoming an enthusiastic substitute for diagnosis.

edits.text: Make clean cuts on either side of the damaged portion and remove that section of washer hose. The illustrated cut-out length is 0.5000 in (12.7 mm).
edits.why: The dimension spans the section between the cut lines. Removing that section leaves the hose ends ready for the adapter.

edits.text: Insert a windshield washer hose adapter between the cut ends. Push each hose end over its corresponding adapter end until seated against the central body, as shown in the assembled view.
edits.why: The adapter bridges the removed section. In the finished drawing, the hose covers the insertion portions on both sides while the adapter's central body remains exposed.

edits.text: NOTE: A difficult repair may also require clamping; use the following branch if necessary.
edits.why: This retains the conditional clamping option rather than making clamps mandatory for every adapter repair.

edits.text: If necessary, fit a segment of black rubber hose with a 6.4 mm (0.25 in) internal diameter over both ends of the washer hose, then secure it with spring clamps.
edits.why: This is the additional sleeve-and-clamp arrangement specified for difficult cases. Keep it conditional; no clamp force or separate operating test is specified.
